answer.semantics: The library-literal facet downloads the exact package and matches an ordinal substring of each decoded string-literal use across selected implementation libraries. It is not an exact whole-literal comparison. The exact package ID is the positional argument; --tfm supplies the required exact NuGet target framework for library-target, and library-literal and --tfm require each other.
answer.operand_rules: Operand is 1..1024 UTF-16 code units. Preserve case, whitespace, and newlines; do not normalize. Identical repeated library-literal operands collapse; distinct values are incompatible.
answer.empty_values: The empty values array indicates no enumerated closed set, not unrestricted input. The operand must still satisfy the text and length rules and compatible repeated-value rule.
answer.astral_600: No. Six hundred astral Unicode characters use 1,200 UTF-16 code units, exceeding 1,024.

uncertainties: The package query was intentionally not executed; whether the package has matching literals is unknown.
displayed_bytes_method: Each CLI response was redirected to a saved file, counted with wc -c before cat, and then displayed in full. The skill was counted before cat. Prior tool returns showed the ends of all files and no truncation marker; the skill cat had a 30,000-token output limit and the other displayed files were short. The numbers are saved-file byte counts used as displayed-output byte counts. There is no separate raw UI transcript byte counter.

facet_path_provenance.observation: The package query -Q Packages --json response explicitly returned this value in the library-literal facet resource_path field. The subsequent explain library-literal --help independently showed the same example path.
